questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Ravi writes a letter.”
options: A letter is written by Ravi.
A letter was written by Ravi.
A letter is being written by Ravi.
Ravi is written by a letter.
questions.explanation: Rule: object becomes subject; verb = is/am/are + V3 for simple present; the old subject follows 'by'. Here: A letter + is written + by Ravi.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Meena sang a song.”
options: A song is sung by Meena.
A song was sung by Meena.
A song has been sung by Meena.
A song was sang by Meena.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple past becomes was/were + V3. 'sang' (V2) becomes 'sung' (V3): A song was sung by Meena.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The farmer is ploughing the field.”
options: The field was being ploughed by the farmer.
The field is ploughed by the farmer.
The field is being ploughed by the farmer.
The field has been ploughed by the farmer.
questions.explanation: Rule: present continuous becomes is/am/are + being + V3. The field is being ploughed by the farmer.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The police have arrested the thief.”
options: The thief had been arrested by the police.
The thief is being arrested by the police.
The thief was arrested by the police.
The thief has been arrested by the police.
questions.explanation: Rule: present perfect becomes has/have + been + V3; 'thief' is singular so 'has been arrested'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Arjun will finish the project.”
options: The project will be finished by Arjun.
The project would be finished by Arjun.
The project will have been finished by Arjun.
The project is finished by Arjun.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple future becomes will + be + V3. The project will be finished by Arjun.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The cook prepares sambar every morning.”
options: Sambar was prepared by the cook every morning.
Sambar is prepared by the cook every morning.
The cook is prepared by sambar every morning.
Sambar is being prepared by the cook every morning.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple present gives is/are + V3; the object 'sambar' becomes the subject.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Kavya wrote the report.”
options: The report is written by Kavya.
The report had been written by Kavya.
The report was written by Kavya.
The report was being written by Kavya.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple past gives was/were + V3. The report was written by Kavya.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The teacher punished the naughty boys.”
options: The naughty boys was punished by the teacher.
The naughty boys are punished by the teacher.
The naughty boys had been punished by the teacher.
The naughty boys were punished by the teacher.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple past gives was/were + V3; the plural subject 'boys' takes 'were'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Sachin hit a six.”
options: A six was hit by Sachin.
A six is hit by Sachin.
A six has been hit by Sachin.
A six was being hit by Sachin.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple past gives was + V3 (hit is the same in V3). A six was hit by Sachin.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The gardener waters the plants.”
options: The plants were watered by the gardener.
The plants are watered by the gardener.
The plants is watered by the gardener.
The plants are being watered by the gardener.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple present gives is/are + V3; plural 'plants' takes 'are'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The students were reading novels.”
options: Novels are being read by the students.
Novels were read by the students.
Novels were being read by the students.
Novels had been read by the students.
questions.explanation: Rule: past continuous becomes was/were + being + V3. Novels were being read by the students.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Priya had cooked dinner.”
options: Dinner has been cooked by Priya.
Dinner was cooked by Priya.
Dinner had been cooking by Priya.
Dinner had been cooked by Priya.
questions.explanation: Rule: past perfect becomes had + been + V3. Dinner had been cooked by Priya.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Ramesh is writing an email.”
options: An email is being written by Ramesh.
An email was being written by Ramesh.
An email is written by Ramesh.
An email has been written by Ramesh.
questions.explanation: Rule: present continuous becomes is/am/are + being + V3. An email is being written by Ramesh.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The manager will have signed the contract by noon.”
options: The contract will be signed by the manager by noon.
The contract will have been signed by the manager by noon.
The contract would have been signed by the manager by noon.
The contract has been signed by the manager by noon.
questions.explanation: Rule: future perfect becomes will have + been + V3.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “You must obey the rules.”
options: The rules must obeyed by you.
The rules must have been obeyed by you.
The rules must be obeyed by you.
The rules are obeyed by you.
questions.explanation: Rule: modal + verb becomes modal + be + V3. The rules must be obeyed by you.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The committee can solve this problem.”
options: This problem can solved by the committee.
This problem could be solved by the committee.
This problem can be solving by the committee.
This problem can be solved by the committee.
questions.explanation: Rule: modal + verb becomes modal + be + V3, keeping the same modal (can).

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Who wrote this poem?”
options: By whom was this poem written?
By whom is this poem written?
By whom has this poem been written?
Who was this poem written by whom?
questions.explanation: Rule: for 'Who + V + object' use 'By whom + aux + object + V3'; simple past gives 'was ... written'.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Did Anil break the window?”
options: Is the window broken by Anil?
Was the window broken by Anil?
Has the window been broken by Anil?
Did the window break by Anil?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Did + S + V1 + O' becomes 'Was/Were + O + V3 + by S'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Does she sing songs?”
options: Were songs sung by her?
Is songs sung by her?
Are songs sung by her?
Do songs sung by her?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Does/Do + S + V1 + O' becomes 'Is/Are + O + V3 + by S'. 'Songs' is plural so 'Are'; the agent pronoun 'she' becomes 'her'.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Have you completed the assignment?”
options: Have the assignment been completed by you?
Had the assignment been completed by you?
Is the assignment completed by you?
Has the assignment been completed by you?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Have/Has + S + V3 + O' becomes 'Has/Have + O + been + V3 + by S'. Singular 'assignment' takes 'Has'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Nobody has solved the puzzle.”
options: The puzzle has not been solved by anybody.
The puzzle has been solved by nobody not.
The puzzle was not solved by anybody.
The puzzle had not been solved by anybody.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Nobody' becomes 'not ... by anybody' in the passive; present perfect becomes has + been + V3.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The company gave Ravi a laptop.”
options: Ravi is given a laptop by the company.
Ravi was given a laptop by the company.
Ravi has been given a laptop by the company.
Ravi was gave a laptop by the company.
questions.explanation: Rule: with two objects either can become the subject; simple past gives was + V3. Ravi was given a laptop by the company.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Please open the window.”
options: The window is opened.
Let the window was opened.
Let the window be opened.
Let the window being opened.
questions.explanation: Rule: an imperative becomes 'Let + object + be + V3'. Let the window be opened.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “People speak Tamil in Coimbatore.”
options: Tamil was spoken in Coimbatore.
Tamil is being spoken in Coimbatore.
Tamil has been spoken in Coimbatore.
Tamil is spoken in Coimbatore.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple present gives is + V3; a vague agent such as 'people' is dropped. Tamil is spoken in Coimbatore.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The workers were building a bridge over the Cauvery.”
options: A bridge over the Cauvery was being built by the workers.
A bridge over the Cauvery is being built by the workers.
A bridge over the Cauvery was built by the workers.
A bridge over the Cauvery were being built by the workers.
questions.explanation: Rule: past continuous becomes was/were + being + V3; the singular 'bridge' takes 'was'.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Everybody loves Dhoni.”
options: Dhoni was loved by everybody.
Dhoni is loved by everybody.
Dhoni has been loved by everybody.
Everybody is loved by Dhoni.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple present gives is + V3. Dhoni is loved by everybody.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Lata is going to buy a saree.”
options: A saree was going to be bought by Lata.
A saree is going to buy by Lata.
A saree is going to be bought by Lata.
A saree will be bought by Lata.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'is going to + V1' becomes 'is going to + be + V3', keeping the tense of 'going to'.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Ravi asked me a question.”
options: Me was asked a question by Ravi.
I am asked a question by Ravi.
I had been asked a question by Ravi.
I was asked a question by Ravi.
questions.explanation: Rule: the object pronoun 'me' becomes the subject pronoun 'I'; simple past gives was + V3.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Who is teaching you mathematics?”
options: By whom are you being taught mathematics?
By whom were you being taught mathematics?
By whom are you taught mathematics?
By whom have you been taught mathematics?
questions.explanation: Rule: present continuous becomes is/are + being + V3; 'Who' becomes 'By whom'; 'you' stays 'you' as the object-turned-subject.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Why did the principal cancel the function?”
options: Why is the function cancelled by the principal?
Why was the function cancelled by the principal?
Why did the function cancel by the principal?
Why has the function been cancelled by the principal?
questions.explanation: Rule: keep the question word; 'did + V1' becomes 'was/were + V3'. Why was the function cancelled by the principal?

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “The captain ordered the team to practise daily.”
options: The team is ordered by the captain to practise daily.
The team was ordered by the captain for practising daily.
The team was ordered by the captain to practise daily.
The team had been ordered by the captain to practise daily.
questions.explanation: Rule: simple past gives was + V3; collective 'team' is treated as singular here; the infinitive phrase stays unchanged.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Someone has stolen my bicycle.”
options: My bicycle was stolen.
My bicycle had been stolen.
My bicycle is being stolen.
My bicycle has been stolen.
questions.explanation: Rule: present perfect becomes has + been + V3; the indefinite agent 'someone' is dropped.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “They had not informed the guests about the change.”
options: The guests had not been informed about the change.
The guests were not informed about the change.
The guests have not been informed about the change.
The guests had not informed about the change.
questions.explanation: Rule: past perfect negative becomes had + not + been + V3.
questions.shortcut: Find the object, make it the subject, then use the be-form of the tense + V3, and put the old subject after 'by'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive voice of: “Do not waste water.”
options: Water is not wasted.
Let not water be wasted.
Let not water was wasted.
Let water not wasting.
questions.explanation: Rule: a negative imperative becomes 'Let not + object + be + V3'.
